How Find text decides what a box is

Every picture below is your own chapter 1, and every number is read out of the code that runs - not typed in by hand.

0

The four answers it can give

BubbleDialogue inside a drawn balloon. The default, and what it falls back to whenever it is unsure.
CaptionNarration boxed off by printed rules - a panel, a title card, a ruled strip.
Outside textWriting lying loose on the artwork with no balloon round it.
Sound effectDrawn, not set. On manhwa and manhua the detector does not produce these at all - you make them with 3.

Caption is a sub-type of bubble in the box list; the detector only ever produces these four and you change any of them with 1, 2 or 3.

1

The page is squeezed into a square first

Before anything looks at your page it is scaled to fit a 1024×1024 box by its longest side and padded with black. This is the single most important thing to know about the whole pipeline: the model never sees your page at full size.

A tall strip loses the most. This is why a page more than 6.0× taller than wide gets a warning in the Find text dialog - past that the labels start coming back wrong.

2

Two different things look for writing

One model, two outputs, and they are good at different things.

Left: the block head draws a rectangle round each run of writing - excellent at set type, and blind to brush-drawn effects. Right: the mask marks every pixel it thinks is writing - it has the 사박 the block head missed entirely.

Where a box came from already decides a lot:

Found byStarts life as
the block headasked the three questions in step 3
the mask, where the block head found nothing sound effect - writing not set in a block is hand-drawn
CRAFT, the second detectorsound effect
3

Question one: is it boxed off by straight lines?

This is asked first, and it has to be. It walks outward from each of the four sides looking for a printed rule.

A side counts when 80% of one row of pixels jumps by 30 grey levels against the next - that is an edge, not a gradient. Find one on 3 of the four sides within 1.2× the box and it is a caption.

Why first: page 006's caption is a white panel on a starfield. Its surroundings are 43% bright against the 45% bar in question two, so the "outside text" answer claimed it before anything else got a look. Measured over the chapter, asking the caption question first never once turned a balloon into a caption.
4

Question two: is there paper around it, or artwork?

Take a ring around the box - 40% of its width and height out on each side - and count how much of that ring is pale (brighter than 200 of 255).

Green is paper, red is artwork. Under 45% paper and the box is called outside text; at or above it, a bubble.

Note the second example is tiny. On your chapter this branch almost never fires - nearly everything is either in a balloon or in a caption panel. It matters much more on pages with shouting laid over the art.
5

Question three: none of the above

If neither test fires, the answer is bubble. That is deliberate: it is the commonest thing on a page, and it is the safest thing to be wrong about - a wrong bubble is one keypress from right, while a missed one has to be noticed first.

The whole of it, in order: straight edge on 3 of 4 sides? ──── yes ──▶ CAPTION │ no ▼ ring under 45% paper? ─────────── yes ──▶ OUTSIDE TEXT │ no ▼ BUBBLE
6

Then the balloon finder gets a second say

After all the boxes exist, a separate pass walks out from each one's ink until it hits the outline drawn around it, and takes the enclosed paper as the balloon - refusing anything that is not flat pale paper with no drawn edges in it.

That shape is what your English gets laid out inside, which is why a balloon matters even when the label was already right.

It can also overrule question two. A box called outside text that turns out to be sitting inside a real balloon is renamed a bubble.

It does not work the other way. Not finding a balloon does not mean there isn't one - this pass deliberately refuses caption panels and anything ragged. Measured over 55 pages, "no balloon found" fires on 54% of all dialogue boxes, so demoting on it would have relabelled half your chapter.
7

Last, what you asked for is kept

The detector reads the whole page whatever you ticked, so the boxes in the Find text dialog are a filter at the end, not a search. Two things are applied here:

your ticksanything whose family you did not ask for is dropped
the formaton manhwa and manhua sound effects are dropped whatever is ticked - half of what came back was artwork

Everything that survives arrives as one of the three main types. Sub-types - thought, aside, angry - are never guessed; they are yours to set.

!

What it never does

Nothing here reads the words, and nothing looks at the drawing. Every answer above comes from measuring the paper around a box: how bright it is, whether there is a straight line near it, whether something encloses it.

Which is also where its mistakes come from. A sound effect drawn across a pale sky has paper all round it and comes back a bubble; a sigh in a balloon and a sigh drawn on the art are the same word and the same shape. The box type is a guess from the paper, and it is one click from right.

Built from the code as it stands: comic-text-detector at 1024px, block confidence 0.4, mask floor 0.2, caption rule 3/4 sides at 1.2× reach, ring bar 45% paper, second detector reach 0.3. Pictures rendered from chapter 1.
